news.casting_brief: Field geochemists, river hydrologists, and climate modelers in remote permafrost terrain; mentor-skeptic dynamic; stakes are global carbon accounting.
news.script_brief: Researchers chasing river greenhouse gas emissions from thawing permafrost stumble on a hidden ally: accelerated rock weathering pulling CO2 from the air. Tension builds as one team insists thaw means pure carbon loss while another proves uptake can fully offset—or surpass—emissions. Beat hooks: the surprise measurement, the regional reversal, the
news.news_close_brief: Scientists report that thawing permafrost can spur rock weathering that absorbs atmospheric CO2, in some regions offsetting or exceeding river greenhouse gas emissions.

dramatic_state.dramatic_question: Will Ned's surprise weathering measurement prove rock CO2 uptake can fully offset—or surpass—the thawing permafrost's river emissions?
dramatic_state.character_a_wants: To broadcast that thawing permafrost means pure CO2 loss, no exceptions
dramatic_state.character_b_wants: To prove accelerated rock weathering uptake offsets the river's carbon emissions
dramatic_state.ending_change: The headline of pure carbon loss flips into a regional reversal as weathering uptake outpaces river CO2 emissions.
